quotes.text: Although the Board's investigation is still on-going and no determination of probable cause has been reached, interim findings in the investigation have revealed a safety issue that warrants attention ... During the wreckage recovery, investigators discovered that gusset plates at eight different joint locations in the main center span were fractured. The Board, with assistance from the FHWA, conducted a thorough review of the design of the bridge, with an emphasis on the design of the gusset plates. This review discovered that the original design process of the I-35W bridge led to a serious error in sizing some of the gusset plates in the main truss.

timeline.event: Construction on the I-35W Mississippi River bridge began.
The bridge was completed and opened to traffic.
A median barrier, larger outside walls, and a thicker concrete deck were added to the bridge, causing additional loading.
Vehicles experienced black ice and a major pile-up occurred on the northbound side when temperatures reached −30 °F (−34 °C).
The federal government gave the I-35W bridge a rating of 'structurally deficient', citing significant corrosion in its bearings.
MnDOT began inspecting the bridge annually.
The bridge was identified as the single most treacherous cold-weather spot in the Twin Cities freeway system due to black ice.
Additional additions including a thicker concrete deck caused additional loading on the gusset plates.
Minnesota DOT began testing magnesium chloride solutions and mixtures to reduce black ice on the bridge.
The state embedded temperature-activated nozzles in the bridge deck to spray potassium acetate solution.
The automated de-icing system came into operation.
A study by the civil engineering department of the University of Minnesota evaluated stress cracking and noted a lack of redundancy in the main truss system.
Inspection photos of the bridge showed gusset-plate bowing.
The bridge was rated 'structurally deficient' and given a sufficiency rating of 50 in the National Bridge Inventory database.
An inspection found problems of cracking and fatigue.
A steel reinforcement project was planned for the bridge.
The steel reinforcement project was canceled after engineers realized drilling for retrofitting would weaken the bridge.
The central span of the bridge suddenly gave way and collapsed into the river and onto the riverbanks, killing 13 people and injuring 145.
timeline.place: I-35W Mississippi River bridge, Minneapolis, Minnesota

timeline.event: An Emergency Operations Center was established in Minneapolis City Hall.
Mayor R. T. Rybak and Governor Tim Pawlenty declared a state of emergency for Minneapolis and the State of Minnesota.
President Bush visited the site and pledged support, announcing Mary Peters would lead the rebuilding effort.
United States Navy divers began arriving to assist local authorities in recovery operations.
President Bush signed into law $250 million in emergency funding passed unanimously by Congress.
The Hennepin County Board of Commissioners voted to request a major disaster declaration from President Bush.
USDOT Secretary Mary Peters announced $50 million in immediate emergency relief and an additional $5 million to reimburse transit operations.
The last victim was recovered from the river, and Governor Pawlenty formally requested a major disaster designation.
President Bush declared an emergency for Minnesota rather than a major disaster, allowing recovery of certain costs through FEMA.
MnDOT announced that Flatiron Construction and Manson Construction Co. would build the replacement bridge for $234 million.
Construction began on the new I-35W bridge after demolition of the collapsed bridge was substantially completed.
The NTSB announced that the original design specified steel gusset plates that were undersized and inadequate.
The NTSB released an update on the investigation detailing gusset-plate bowing seen in June 2003 inspection photos.
The state of Minnesota reached a $38 million agreement to compensate victims of the bridge collapse.
The replacement I-35W Saint Anthony Falls Bridge opened to the public at 5 a.m.
The NTSB released the final findings of its investigation, citing undersized gusset plates as the primary cause of the collapse.
The last lawsuits against URS Corporation were settled for $52.4 million.

legacy.what: The FHWA advised states to inspect 700 U.S. bridges of similar construction after a possible design flaw related to gusset plates was identified.
The replacement structure, the I-35W Saint Anthony Falls Bridge, opened to the public on September 18.
The state legislature increased the Minnesota state fuel tax by $0.055 per gallon via a veto override to fund MnDOT maintenance.
The state of Minnesota reached a $38 million agreement to compensate victims of the bridge collapse.
The last of the lawsuits against URS Corporation were settled for $52.4 million.
